KnowledgeArticle.Title: Broken Sidewalk
KnowledgeArticle.Description: Report a sidewalk condition that may cause a trip hazard. Learn about how to maintain or repair the sidewalk next to your property.

Section.Name: Broken Sidewalk Intro
Section.Content:
Need something else?

  • Trees and Sidewalks Repair to request free repair for sidewalks that are damaged by curbside tree roots
  • Sidewalk Collapsed to report a sidewalk that has caved-in or fallen into a deep hole
  • Sidewalk Violation and Repair to learn about repairing or clearing a sidewalk violation from your property or getting a status/copy of a violation
  • Sidewalk Utility Hardware Complaint

Property owners are responsible for installing, maintaining, and repairing the sidewalks adjacent to their properties. 

Learn about sidewalk repair.

The Department of Transportation's (DOT) goal is to make the City's sidewalks safe for pedestrians and help prevent trip hazards. DOT inspects sidewalk conditions not caused by tree roots.

A sidewalk condition includes:  

  • Loose, cracked, uneven, or missing sections
  • Improper slope causing drainage issues
  • Patchwork or hardware sticking out

Learn about common sidewalk defects.

You can report a broken sidewalk. For sidewalk conditions not caused by tree roots, DOT will inspect the location and notify the property owner.

You can report a sidewalk condition located:

  • Next to a residential or commercial property
  • Next to a vacant lot
  • Next to City-owned property
  • At an extended sidewalk at a bus stop 
  • Under a bridge or on a traffic median

An exact street address for the sidewalk defect is required for all reports.

Section.Name: 1, 2 and 3 Family Residential Properties
Section.Content:
Property owners are responsible for installing, maintaining, and repairing the sidewalks adjacent to their properties except for sidewalks damaged by tree roots. 

Sidewalk Damaged by Tree Roots

If the sidewalk in front of the 1-, 2-, or 3-family residential property is damaged due to tree roots, it may qualify for free repair through the Parks Department Trees and Sidewalks Repair Program.

To make a repair request, visit the Trees and Sidewalks Repair page instead.

Sidewalk Not Damaged by Tree Roots

If the damaged or broken sidewalk next to the property is not caused by tree roots, the Department of Transportation (DOT) will inspect the sidewalk complaint. If warranted, a Notice of Violation will be sent to the property owner.

ContentAction.Name: Broken Sidewalk Next to Residential Property with 1-3 Units

Section.Name: Residential Property (4+ Units), Commercial Property, or Vacant Lot
Section.Content:
Property owners are responsible for installing, maintaining and repairing the sidewalks adjacent to their properties, including tree root damage. 

You can report a broken sidewalk next to:

  • Residential properties with four or more units
  • Residential properties with at least one commercial space
  • Commercial properties
  • Vacant lots

The Department of Transportation will inspect the sidewalk complaint. If warranted, a Notice of Sidewalk Violation will be sent to the property owner.

ContentAction.Name: Broken Sidewalk Next to Residential Property (4+ Units), Commercial Property, or Vacant Lot

Section.Name: City-Owned Property
Section.Content:
The City is responsible for installing, maintaining, and repairing the sidewalks adjacent to City-owned property.

You can report a broken sidewalk next to:

  • Public housing
  • Public hospitals
  • Public parks (perimeter only)
  • Public schools
  • Public shelters
  • Libraries
  • City agency office buildings
  • Any other City-Owned property

The Department of Transportation will verify that it is City-owned property and will inspect the sidewalk. If installation, maintenance, or repairs are required, the responsible agency will be notified.

ContentAction.Name: Broken Sidewalk Next to City-owned Property

Section.Name: Extended Sidewalk at a Bus Stop
Section.Content:
You can report an extended sidewalk platform that is broken or missing.

An extended sidewalk is the widening of the sidewalk platforms typically located at select bus stops.

They provide a raised area, allowing the bus to pull up alongside smoothly without needing to merge in and out of traffic. The materials are usually rubber texture in black with white markings.

ContentAction.Name: Broken or Missing Extended Sidewalk Platform at Bus Stop

Section.Name: Under a Bridge or on a Traffic Median
Section.Content:
The Department of Transportation (DOT) maintains many of the overpasses (bridges) and traffic medians for City roadways and highways.

Complaints about a damaged sidewalk, including tree root damage, under an overpass or on a traffic median or island are accepted.

DOT will verify that it is City-owned property and will inspect the sidewalk. If installation, maintenance, or repairs are required, the responsible agency or entity will be notified.

ContentAction.Name: Broken Sidewalk Under Bridge or on Traffic Median

Section.Name: Damage Caused by Another Party
Section.Content:
As the property owner, you are responsible for building or repairing the sidewalks next to your property and maintaining them in a reasonably safe condition. Regardless of what or who caused the damage, you will be liable for any violations and fines accrued by the damaged sidewalks.

If the sidewalk was broken by someone or something else:

  • Document the damage and source of the damage.
  • If you do not know the source of the damage, the borough's Permit Office can do a search of construction permits issued on the property for a small fee. The Permit Office's telephone number is on the back of the Notice of Violation.
  • Repair and restore the broken sidewalk flags to avoid future violations.
  • Retain receipts documenting the cost of the repair and restoration.
  • Seek repayment of the repair costs from the responsible party. 
  • If the damage was done by a City worker or contractor working for the City, you may file a claim against the City. To learn more, go to the City Claim page.
  • If the damage was done by a utility or private contractor, you should seek repayment from them.
